subject: Transportation Systems
title: New York's Subway Debut
description: A 60-second lesson on New York's Subway Debut.

hook.text: New York's subway opened in 1904. On day one, 150,000 people crammed in to try it.

buildup.text: The city was desperate. Elevated trains were noisy and streetcars couldn't handle the crowds.

discovery.text: Engineers built a four-track main line—two for local stops, two for express. Nobody had done that.

twist.text: The original fare was five cents. It stayed five cents for 44 years, slowly bankrupting the system.

climax.text: Today the NYC subway runs 24/7 across 472 stations—one of the few metros that never sleeps.

punchline.text: New York built the subway that never closes.

quiz.question: What made New York's original subway design innovative?
